notes.title: Summerhill, One Year Later 🐑
notes.content:
On the 8th of June 2023, after many years of preparation, we announced our brand-new sheep herding puzzle-adventure game, Summerhill, during the [url=https://youtu.be/rDIOeEWaloc]Day of the Devs: Summer Games Fest Edition[/url] showcase.

For almost 10 years, we’ve been known exclusively as the developers of the [url=https://youtu.be/WGFpyjygANw]Alto’s Adventure[/url] series, so it’s been thrilling to finally start talking about our next project as a studio.

[previewyoutube=o7hDHyo5Q_I;full][/previewyoutube]
One year later, and we’re still hard at work crafting the world of Summerhill - our most ambitious project to date. While there will be much more to share in the future, for now we thought we’d give you a small recap of what we’ve been up to.

We’ve been visiting various game industry events, to chat with our peers about the world we are crafting. Our studio has expanded, assembling a crew of talented and experienced game devs from around the world, each of whom has been instrumental in bringing Summerhill to life. You can meet a few of them in our latest [url=https://x.com/landandseagames/status/1807776250666099159]team introductions here[/url].

Towards the end of 2023, we teased a fresh take on Summerhill through a new piece of artwork created by the exceedingly talented [url=https://www.instagram.com/_alariko/]Alarkio[/url], who you may recognise from his very popular series of paintings and illustrations on social media. We look forward to continuing to work with Alariko as we bring Summerhill to life!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224900/75900a411949c28d24680ffa61c3422a6dfb06ea.png[/img]
The eagle-eyed among you may have spotted we’ve already given Summerhill’s Steam page a new lick of paint, featuring Alariko’s artwork 👀.

Outside the world of Summerhill, we released a special version of [url=https://x.com/landandseagames/status/1759980955895267345]Alto’s Odyssey: The Lost City for Apple Vision Pro[/url], and in case you missed it, we brought [url=http://s.team/a/2837600]The Alto Collection to Steam[/url] - where it feels right at home on Steam Deck!

Last but not least, we wanted to give a heartfelt thank you to everyone who’s joined us on Summerhill’s journey so far. Since we announced last year, we’ve received a lot of excitement and enthusiasm for the game, which has given us a great deal of encouragement as we carry on with development ♥️.

You can keep up-to-date on Summerhill (and say hello to us!) by joining us on [url=https://x.com/landandseagames]Twitter / X[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/landandseagames/]Instagram[/url], [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@landandseagames]TikTok[/url], [url=https://www.threads.net/@landandseagames]Threads[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/@landandseagames/]YouTube[/url]. If you like very infrequent, longer form reads, you can also [url=https://www.summerhill.game/#MailingList]join our mailing list[/url].

Most importantly, if you haven’t done so already, please make sure to add Summerhill to your Steam wishlist. Doing so will ensure you receive the biggest (and most exciting!) news about the game, and you will be notified when the game releases. As a small studio, it’s by far the most impactful way you can support our team, as wishlists help us reach a wider audience that may be interested in our sheep herding, coming-of-age folktale. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2324410/Summerhill/

We cannot wait to share Summerhill with you all ♥️ 🐑.

Best wishes,
The Land & Sea Team.

notes.title: We just announced our next game – Summerhill, at the Day of the Devs showcase!
notes.content:
Hi there!

We’re Land & Sea, the small UK-based development team best known for our previous titles [url=https://altosadventure.com/]Alto’s Adventure[/url] and [url=https://altosodyssey.com/]Alto’s Odyssey[/url]. If you’re reading this, there’s a fair chance that you’ve ended up here because of our recent announcement included in the Day of the Devs Summer Game Fest showcase – during which we announced our next project, a sheep herding puzzle-adventure game called Summerhill!

If you didn’t happen to catch the Summer Game Fest livestream last Thursday, you can check out our 4k teaser trailer below, or watch our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rDIOeEWaloc&ab_channel=thegameawards]full feature here[/url] – in which our Creative Director Harry Nesbitt covers the history of our studio and inspiration behind Summerhill itself – hosted on The Game Awards YouTube channel.

[previewyoutube=o7hDHyo5Q_I;full][/previewyoutube]

After many years of preparation, we’re excited to be able to tell you more about the world we are constructing. In short, Summerhill is a story-driven puzzle adventure in which you will play as a young shepherd and their dog. Together you’ll be tasked with rescuing your lost sheep and uncovering the long-forgotten mysteries of an ancient landscape.

The gameplay of Summerhill is primarily centred around seeking out and herding your sheep to safety through vibrant lands scattered with ruined contraptions that stand in your way. As the journey continues, you will forge a deep bond with your sheepdog, working together to solve increasingly challenging puzzles and find the path ahead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224900/f55fe17d1ff6a187e6c9e3e8cfaa39cdbb399737.png[/img]

The idea for Summerhill was first conceived back in 2017. At the time, the team was searching for a playful and satisfying game mechanic with a grounded “folk” sensibility. We were particularly drawn to the rich history and cultural impact of sheep herding – a theme we touched on lightly in Alto’s Adventure (Alto himself being a humble llama shepherd) but that we always felt had more unexplored potential.

We realised there had never been a game that really tapped into what it means to be a shepherd, as sheep are often used as a throwaway gag, or depicted in a cutesy, cartoonish way. We felt that this kind of levity tended to undermine the benevolent, enigmatic nature and deep historic relationship sheep share with humankind, so we set out to put our own grounded spin on this dynamic.

During early investigations, we quickly realised that we wanted to explore the intrinsic ‘flow’ that is present in the movement of a flock of sheep. Using our experience creating balletic gameplay through the snowboarding mechanics of the Alto titles, we set about aiming to capture the grace and fluidity of sheep flocking from one space to another, which has now solidified as a central pillar of the game. 

While there’s much more we hope to share in future, we hope this glimpse into the origins and themes of Summerhill gives you some idea of what to expect from the game down the track!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44224900/d22429e40368931779e3ec2b85d973532b497d13.png[/img]

Lastly, we want to say a hearty thank you to anyone who has joined us on our journey! Our announcement has been a long time coming and truly is a huge milestone for us, but there’s still a long road ahead. If you like what you have seen of Summerhill so far, Wishlisting the game here on Steam is by far the most impactful way you can support our little indie team. It really helps us reach more people who might be interested in the world we are crafting!

We’ll be posting more updates of our progress over the coming months, so be sure to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/landandseagames]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/landandseagames/]Instagram[/url] or [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@landandseagames]TikTok[/url], and join our [url=https://www.summerhill.game/#MailingList]mailing list[/url] to be the first to learn more.

Kind regards,
The Land & Sea Team
